inverse: "notes": "The Marian antiphon of Paschaltide, which stands from Compline of Holy Saturday to the Saturday after Pentecost — after the Ave Regína cælorum of Lent, before the Salve Regína of the season after Pentecost, with the versicle that follows it. Four lines, each sealed with an allelúia, and two more in the versicle: the word is Hebrew, indeclinable, and this edition prints it with i where witness do prints j, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. The syntax turns on one construction a reader will not guess: DEUM at w017 is the object of ORA at w014, because Latin oro governs the one entreated in the accusative. The line therefore holds both a person prayed TO and, in pro + ablative, the people prayed FOR — it asks God on our behalf, and does not ask for God. QUEM at w006 has no antecedent in the text at all; the antiphon says who it is only by what he did, and both witnesses leave it so. No speaker is recorded: the Marian antiphon file marks the versicle v./R., and outside the Mass this edition reads those as the shape of a versicle rather than as officers (SCHEMA.md).",
